translationRepairs: In the eleventh month, on gengyin, clansmen who had held princely commandery titles were reduced to county marquises; only a few with outstanding merit kept their ranks.
In the eleventh month, on gengyin, clansmen who had held princely commandery titles were reduced to county dukes; only a few with outstanding merit kept their ranks.
縣公 is the rank of county duke; the draft mistranslates it as "county marquises".
In the twelfth month, on jisi, Grand Protector of Yizhou Dou Gui reported that the Liao had rebelled and asked to send troops against them.
In the twelfth month, on jisi, Grand Area Commander of Yizhou Dou Gui reported that the Liao had rebelled and asked to send troops against them.
大都督 is Grand Area Commander, the regional military-administrative office, not "Grand Protector".
Thereupon he dropped the conscription of middle-aged youths and rewarded Wei Zheng with a golden jar.
Thereupon he dropped the conscription of middle youths and rewarded Wei Zheng with a golden jar.
中男 is the statutory category of "middle youths" (males under eighteen); the draft wrongly renders it "middle-aged youths".

A clerk in the Department of Reception accepted one bolt of silk. The emperor wanted to execute him, but Pei Ju, minister of the Ministry of Revenue, remonstrated: "An official who accepts a bribe surely deserves death;

A clerk of the Bureau of Gate Control accepted one bolt of silk. The emperor wanted to execute him, but Pei Ju, minister of the Ministry of Revenue, remonstrated: "An official who accepts a bribe surely deserves death;
司門令史 is a clerk of the Bureau of Gate Control (司門) in the Ministry of Justice, not the "Department of Reception".
In the sixth month, on xinsi, Feng Deyi, Right Director of the Department of State Affairs and Duke of Mimeng, died.
In the sixth month, on xinsi, Feng Deyi, Right Director of the Department of State Affairs and Duke Ming of Mi, died.
密明公 combines the fief Mi (密) with the posthumous name Ming (明), i.e. Duke Ming of Mi; the draft fuses them into "Duke of Mimeng".
When someone reported that Youliang harbored treasonous ambitions, Emperor Taizong sent Chief Director of the Secretariat Yuwen Shiji by fast courier to replace him and investigate the charges.
When someone reported that Youliang harbored treasonous ambitions, Emperor Taizong sent Director of the Secretariat Yuwen Shiji by fast courier to replace him and investigate the charges.
中書令 is Director of the Secretariat; "Chief Director" adds a rank not in the source.

On xinyou, Yuwen Shiji was dismissed as Chief Director of the Secretariat and appointed director of the Palace Domestic Service, while Du Yan, chief imperial censor, was brought in to participate in deliberations on state affairs.

On xinyou, Yuwen Shiji was dismissed as Director of the Secretariat and appointed director of the Palace Domestic Service, while Du Yan, chief imperial censor, was brought in to participate in deliberations on state affairs.
中書令 is Director of the Secretariat; "Chief Director" adds a rank not in the source.

In winter, the tenth month, on yiyou, he dispatched Li Gongyan, vice director of the Scattered Cavalry, with imperial credentials to offer reassurance. Feng Ang sent his son Zhizai to accompany the envoy to court.

In winter, the tenth month, on yiyou, he dispatched Li Gongyan, vice director of the Scattered Cavalry, with imperial credentials to offer reassurance. Feng Ang sent his son Zhidai to accompany the envoy to court.
智戴 is romanized Zhidai; the draft misreads 戴 as "zai".
On this account his sentence was reduced from death, and he was exiled to Xun Prefecture.
On this account his sentence was reduced from death, and he was exiled to Xi Prefecture.
巂州 is Xi Prefecture (Xīzhōu) in the southwest; the draft misreads it as "Xun".

Vice Minister of Justice Sun Fuga warned Renshi: "You have cleared many prisoners; who among men does not cling to life? I fear that when they see their fellows go free, they will refuse to accept guilt—I worry deeply for you."

Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review Sun Fuga warned Renshi: "You have cleared many prisoners; who among men does not cling to life? I fear that when they see their fellows go free, they will refuse to accept guilt—I worry deeply for you."
大理少卿 is Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review (大理寺), not a Ministry of Justice post.
Liu Ziyi of Jinling, former Sui Director of the Secretariat, was a learned and upright man of stern character; when friends erred, he often rebuked them to their faces.
Liu Ziyi of Jinling, former Sui Director of the Palace Library, was a learned and upright man of stern character; when friends erred, he often rebuked them to their faces.
秘書監 is Director of the Palace Library (秘書省), not the Secretariat.
When Qaghan Tongyehu's power waned, Yishibo's grandson Yinan led his tribe of more than seventy thousand households and submitted to Qaghan Jiali.
When Qaghan Tongyehu's power waned, Yishibo's grandson Yinan led his tribe of more than seventy thousand households and submitted to Qaghan Jieli.
頡利 is romanized Jieli elsewhere in the chapter; "Jiali" is a misspelling of the same khagan.
Jiali's rule fell into disorder, and the Xueyantuo, Huihe, Bayegu, and others rose in rebellion under their leaders.
Jieli's rule fell into disorder, and the Xueyantuo, Huihe, Bayegu, and others rose in rebellion under their leaders.
頡利 is romanized Jieli elsewhere in the chapter; "Jiali" is a misspelling of the same khagan.
Jiali sent his nephew Yugu She with one hundred thousand horsemen to suppress them. The Huihe chieftain Pusa led five thousand riders and routed them at Mount Majie.
Jieli sent his nephew Yugu She with one hundred thousand horsemen to suppress them. The Huihe chieftain Pusa led five thousand riders and routed them at Mount Majie.
頡利 is romanized Jieli elsewhere in the chapter; "Jiali" is a misspelling of the same khagan.
The Xueyantuo also defeated his four military governors, and Jiali could no longer control them.
The Xueyantuo also defeated his four military governors, and Jieli could no longer control them.
頡利 is romanized Jieli elsewhere in the chapter; "Jiali" is a misspelling of the same khagan.
Jiali's power waned further, and his people scattered.
Jieli's power waned further, and his people scattered.
頡利 is romanized Jieli elsewhere in the chapter; "Jiali" is a misspelling of the same khagan.

Heavy snow fell, burying the plains several chi deep; countless sheep and horses perished, and famine spread among the people. Fearing that Tang would exploit his weakness, Jiali led troops to the border of Shuozhou, proclaiming a hunting expedition while in fact preparing for defense.

Heavy snow fell, burying the plains several chi deep; countless sheep and horses perished, and famine spread among the people. Fearing that Tang would exploit his weakness, Jieli led troops to the border of Shuozhou, proclaiming a hunting expedition while in fact preparing for defense.
頡利 is romanized Jieli elsewhere in the chapter; "Jiali" is a misspelling of the same khagan.

Jiali did not want China to ally with Tong Yehu by marriage. He repeatedly sent raiders across the border and also sent word to Tong Yehu: "If you are to escort the Tang princess, you must pass through my lands."

Jieli did not want China to ally with Tong Yehu by marriage. He repeatedly sent raiders across the border and also sent word to Tong Yehu: "If you are to escort the Tang princess, you must pass through my lands."
頡利 is romanized Jieli elsewhere in the chapter; "Jiali" is a misspelling of the same khagan.

Earlier, the Turk qaghan Tuli had set up his headquarters just north of You Prefecture, governing the eastern territories. Dozens of tribes, including the Xi and their allies, largely broke from the Turks and submitted to Tang. Jiali blamed Tuli for losing his followers.

Earlier, the Turk qaghan Tuli had set up his headquarters just north of You Prefecture, governing the eastern territories. Dozens of tribes, including the Xi and their allies, largely broke from the Turks and submitted to Tang. Jieli blamed Tuli for losing his followers.
頡利 is romanized Jieli elsewhere in the chapter; "Jiali" is a misspelling of the same khagan.
When the Xueyantuo, Huihe, and others defeated Yugu She, Jiali sent Tuli to punish them. Tuli's army was beaten again, and he fled back with a small escort.
When the Xueyantuo, Huihe, and others defeated Yugu She, Jieli sent Tuli to punish them. Tuli's army was beaten again, and he fled back with a small escort.
頡利 is romanized Jieli elsewhere in the chapter; "Jiali" is a misspelling of the same khagan.
Jiali flew into a rage, held him for more than ten days, and had him whipped. Tuli nursed a grievance and secretly planned to break with Jiali.
Jieli flew into a rage, held him for more than ten days, and had him whipped. Tuli nursed a grievance and secretly planned to break with Jieli.
頡利 is romanized Jieli elsewhere in the chapter; "Jiali" is a misspelling of the same khagan.
Jiali repeatedly demanded troops from Tuli, but Tuli refused and petitioned to come to court in person.
Jieli repeatedly demanded troops from Tuli, but Tuli refused and petitioned to come to court in person.
頡利 is romanized Jieli elsewhere in the chapter; "Jiali" is a misspelling of the same khagan.
Jiali sent troops against Tuli. On dinghai, Tuli sent an envoy begging for help.
Jieli sent troops against Tuli. On dinghai, Tuli sent an envoy begging for help.
頡利 is romanized Jieli elsewhere in the chapter; "Jiali" is a misspelling of the same khagan.
Yet Jiali too is bound to him by alliance. What then?"
Yet Jieli too is bound to him by alliance. What then?"
頡利 is romanized Jieli elsewhere in the chapter; "Jiali" is a misspelling of the same khagan.

Jiali sent an envoy offering to exchange Liang Shidu for the Khitan. The emperor told the envoy: "The Khitan and the Turks are not the same people. They have just submitted to us—why should I hand them over!

Jieli sent an envoy offering to exchange Liang Shidu for the Khitan. The emperor told the envoy: "The Khitan and the Turks are not the same people. They have just submitted to us—why should I hand them over!
頡利 is romanized Jieli elsewhere in the chapter; "Jiali" is a misspelling of the same khagan.
On guichou, Tuyuhun raided Min Prefecture. Protector-general Li Daoyan repulsed them.
On guichou, Tuyuhun raided Min Prefecture. Area Commander Li Daoyan repulsed them.
都督 here is the prefectural area commander of Minzhou, not a protector-general (都護).
The emperor sent Right Guard General Chai Shao and Palace Supervisor Xue Wanjun to attack him, and ordered Min and the others to hold the eastern city of Shuofang and tighten the pressure.

The emperor sent Grand General of the Right Guard Chai Shao and Palace Supervisor Xue Wanjun to attack him, and ordered Min and the others to hold the eastern city of Shuofang and tighten the pressure.
右衛大將軍 is Grand General of the Right Guard; the draft drops 大 (grand).

In the seventh month of autumn, an edict ordered that Yuwen Huaji's partisans—Niu Fangyu, prefect of Lai Prefecture; Xue Shiliang, prefect of Jiang Prefecture; Tang Fengyi, chief secretary of the Guangzhou military governor; and Yuan Li, Sui Wuya Langjiang—all struck from the rolls and exiled to the frontier.

In the seventh month of autumn, an edict ordered that Yuwen Huaji's partisans—Niu Fangyu, prefect of Lai Prefecture; Xue Shiliang, prefect of Jiang Prefecture; Tang Fengyi, chief secretary of the Guangzhou military governor; and Yuan Li, Sui Gentleman-General of the Martial Fang—all struck from the rolls and exiled to the frontier.
隋武牙郎將 is an office title, Gentleman-General of the Martial Fang; the draft leaves it as untranslated "Wuya Langjiang".
What I hold to is only the Way of Yao, Shun, the Zhou, and Confucius. I regard it as birds having wings and fish having water: lose it and one dies—it cannot be briefly done without."
What I hold to is only the Way of Yao, Shun, the Duke of Zhou, and Confucius. I regard it as birds having wings and fish having water: lose it and one dies—it cannot be briefly done without."
周、孔 pairs the Duke of Zhou with Confucius; the draft renders 周 as the dynasty "the Zhou".

Supervising Censor in charge of recording conduct Du Zhenglun said: "My duty is to record speech. If Your Majesty's words go astray, I must write them down—not only might they harm the present, but they may also invite ridicule from posterity."

Supervising Secretary in charge of recording conduct Du Zhenglun said: "My duty is to record speech. If Your Majesty's words go astray, I must write them down—not only might they harm the present, but they may also invite ridicule from posterity."
給事中 is the Supervising Secretary of the Chancellery, not a censorate post.
